question: When an MCP server widens the inputSchema of an already-approved tool (tools/list_changed, same name and description), does the client (a) silently use the new definition, (b) flag any definition change (pinning / drift detection), (c) re-approve only on an incompatible change, or (d) reason about whether authority widened?
counting_unit: 8 products: 3 SDK families (MCP TypeScript, MCP Python, Vercel AI), 4 host applications (VS Code, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor), 1 scanner (mcp-scan / Snyk agent-scan)

evidence_levels.source: source code read at the cited tag/commit

products.behaviour: default: notification not surfaced; opt-in listChanged.tools.onChanged delivers the refreshed list; no diff, no approval; the widened call reaches the server

the notification reaches the application only through a user-installed message handler; list_tools returns the widened schema under the same name; no diff, no approval; the widened call reaches the server

default: tools/list_changed surfaces only as an 'Unsupported message type' error to onUncaughtError; tools() returns fresh definitions; opt-in fingerprintTools/detectToolDrift (since ai 7.0.19) reports read_file as changed, i.e. that a definition changed, not whether authority widened

re-lists on list_changed; a changed definition is re-registered under the same id (derived from the name only), so per-tool approvals survive; confirmation is per call; server trust is re-asked only when the launch configuration changes
documented to refresh capabilities on list_changed; permission rules match tool names; no documented re-approval on a definition change (not runtime-tested)
per-tool Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked; list_changed and definition changes not documented
approval before MCP tool use by default; allowlist entries are server:tool name patterns; list_changed and definition changes not documented

products.version: mcp-scan 0.4.2 (last release under that name); pinning present up to agent-scan 0.4.5, removed in 0.4.6 (2026-03-11); snyk-agent-scan 0.6.8 has none
products.behaviour: a schema-only widening raises no W003; a description-only change raises W003
products.class: b for descriptions, a for input schemas

finding: none of the 8 products re-approves an approved tool when its input schema widens; one offers opt-in drift detection that flags any change; one pinned descriptions only; two are undocumented

runtime_tests.sdk_diff_or_approval_api: none (consent is left to the host application)
none (consent is left to the host application)
none (consent is left to the host application)
none (consent is left to the host application)
